facts.raw_span: pink-purple dermal papules
polyarticular inflammatory arthritis involving the wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, and proximal interphalangeal joints
fatigue
dyspnea on exertion
5-7 kg weight loss
no fever or sweats
relieved by daily oral prednisone and flared with taper below 10 mg
no lymphadenopathy
nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate (H&E stain)
admixed atypical, irregularly contoured lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes
low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal (20x magnification)
mild restrictive disease with decreased forced vital capacity and total lung capacity

rationales.F01: Pink-purple dermal papules are characteristic of cutaneous lymphomas, particularly mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome.
rationales.F02: Polyarticular inflammatory arthritis is a common feature of rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis.
rationales.F09: Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate is a hallmark of cutaneous lymphomas.
rationales.F10: Admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes are characteristic of cutaneous lymphomas, particularly mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome.
rationales.F11: Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal are characteristic of certain cutaneous lymphomas, particularly mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, along with the low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal, strongly supports Mycosis fungoides. The matching clonal rearrangements in skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample further confirm this diagnosis.
